description: Phase 8 evidence: Pixel Studio — the editor, its authored format, persistence, the animation contract extension, and the measured cost of a user looping animation on the production dashboard.

editor.entry: Locker -> Identity -> Studio Hub -> Companion -> Open Pixel Studio
editor.exposedInternals: none — no planes, anchors, coordinates, asset ids, JSON or matrix sizes on screen
editor.drawingModel: One canvas at the authored grid size, enlarged by CSS with image-rendering pixelated. Nothing is stored per cell in React state.
editor.input: Pointer events, so mouse/touch/pen share one path; touch-action none; pointer capture
editor.fill: iterative and bounded by the cell count, so it cannot recurse or run away

verifiedInBrowser.onion: toggling twice left the drawing byte-identical

threeConceptsKeptDistinct.productionCardSize: the rendering surface; not the editor concern
threeConceptsKeptDistinct.enforcement: a test asserts the serialised creation contains no zoom and that two drafts at different zooms are the same document

timeline.reorder: buttons rather than drag, so it is reachable by keyboard
timeline.duration: 60–1000ms in the editor, 60–2000ms in the format
timeline.onionSkin: previous frame at 28%, next at 16%, drawn as a wash and never written to the draft
timeline.editorPlayback: one setTimeout per frame, not a frame loop

contractExtension.mismatch: A PixelAsset was static, so an animation could only be one plane per frame (defeating plane selection) or a second content kind with its own renderer (forbidden).
extension: geometry: animated with frames[] and optional order[]
contractExtension.whyFramesOnGeometry: so a hand-authored asset with several planes could animate one of them, and neither case is special
contractExtension.paletteModeReason: found by testing: under the strict default a creation became invalid the moment its last pixel of a colour was erased. A scholar palette is a tool, not a description. The strict default is unchanged for built-in assets.

authoredFormat.name: PixelCreation
authoredFormat.pixels: palette indices as digits, . transparent — a 64x64 16-frame drawing fits the payload bound
authoredFormat.direction: one-way: creation -> asset. A test asserts a built-in asset is not a drawable creation.

persistence.model: PixelCreation (userId, slug, name, grid, version, data Json)
whyNotCharacterConfig: Size: up to ~70KB of artwork, and characterConfig is read by useDashboardData, the stats route, conversation payloads and profile views.
Ownership: a creation is a thing a scholar has, in possibly several instances, independent of what they wear. characterConfig records a choice, so it references one by id.
persistence.whyJsonDocument: frames are small, self-contained, always read together, and their shape is owned by the Pixel Display contract; normalising would spread a content format across the schema.

validation.layering: the client validator gates the save button; the API refuses with per-problem reasons before storing; the decoder is total and never throws, so half-typed input cannot crash the editor

playback.onceBehaves: plays through, parks on its final frame, and returns to zero work by itself
playback.notWiredToSystemSignals: a saved animation is not a response to task completion, level-up or AI-thinking
playback.staticAssetsUnaffected: a test asserts a static asset reports no animation at all

defectsFoundByMeasurement.detail: update() returned true whenever the animation was unfinished, which asks for another frame immediately. A 400ms frame produced hundreds of frames of work to hold one picture.
defectsFoundByMeasurement.measured: 181 frames over 3008ms (~60 fps) for a two-frame loop at 400/240ms.
defectsFoundByMeasurement.fix: when a frame is not due, return false so the runtime settles to idle, and schedule one timer for the remaining duration.

defectsFoundByMeasurement.detail: the new timer called requestFrame(), the explicit external wake-up, which reopened a suspended session.
defectsFoundByMeasurement.measured: 9 frames over 3 seconds in a hidden tab.
defectsFoundByMeasurement.fix: requestFrameFromContent() refuses while a suspension is in force. requestFrame() still wakes the display, because a dev control or a test doing so is a different intention — an existing Phase 1 test asserts exactly that, which is how the distinction was found rather than invented.

productionPerformance.scene: a two-frame creation at 400ms + 240ms, equipped, on the real 110px dashboard card
productionPerformance.conclusion: the loop costs what its frames say and nothing more, and every zero-work path returns

preview.sharedPath: both previews go through the production card and the same resolver the dashboard uses
preview.whyTheCardPreviewMatters: Phase 7 O15 established that artwork which looks good enlarged can fail at 110px

customizerIntegration.flow: Create in Studio -> Save -> appears in the Customizer -> Equip -> dashboard renders it
customizerIntegration.namespace: the registry claims user:, so a creation resolves like any other form key
customizerIntegration.fallback: a missing, corrupt or unsupported creation degrades to the built-in character and is reported — verified with an equipped id that does not exist: a valid companion, 438 lit cells

accessibility.layout: below 1000px the controls move under the canvas in one column; the canvas reflows rather than shrinking
accessibility.toolRow: horizontally scrollable so primary tools stay reachable with a thumb
accessibility.keyboard: tools, palette, frames, reorder, playback, zoom and save are all buttons with visible focus rings
accessibility.reducedMotion: verified under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — the preview renders and selection stays legible

openDecisions.O25: New: whether a scholar may author more than a base character. Studio deliberately creates base characters only.
openDecisions.O26: New: whether creations should be shareable. A creation is private to its scholar; sharing is a social feature with its own moderation surface.
openDecisions.O27: New and the honest gap: reduced motion is respected in the editor, but an equipped looping creation still loops on the dashboard. The smallest correct behaviour is probably to hold the first frame under prefers-reduced-motion, and it should be decided with a scholar view of it rather than assumed.
openDecisions.O1_O15: Better informed: a user-facing density choice now exists end to end, and the 110px preview gives art production somewhere to check readability before shipping a form.

limits: One editor, one asset kind: a creation is a base character and nothing else is authorable yet.
QA wrote one creation to one account and removed it afterwards, restoring that account configuration. No other data was touched.
One editing session was walked end to end by hand; the tool behaviours themselves are covered by direct tests.
